function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a convenient online option. | Option | What it offers | How to get it | Tips | |--------|----------------|---------------|------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often handmade cakes; great for custom designs | Search “bakery near me” on Google Maps or Yelp, or ask friends for recommendations | Call ahead to confirm availability and place a custom order. | | **Grocery stores** | Ready‑made cakes, sometimes custom orders | Visit the bakery section in supermarkets like Walmart, Kroger, Publix, or Target | Many have online ordering for pickup or delivery. | | **Specialty cake shops** | Custom cakes, themed designs, premium ingredients | Look up “custom cake shop” + your city; many have websites or Instagram pages | Bring a clear idea of size, flavor, and design; ask about pricing tiers. | | **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide delivery, wide variety of flavors | Sites/apps:
• **Amazon** (Prime Now for same‑day)
• **Bakery.com**
• **Cake Delivery** (e.g., )
• **Etsy** (handmade custom cakes) | Check delivery times, shipping fees, and reviews. | | **Food‑delivery platforms** | Cakes from local restaurants/bakeries delivered to your door | DoorDash, Uber Eats, Postmates, Grubhub – search “cake” or “dessert” | Delivery fees apply; some platforms offer free delivery for orders over a certain amount. | | **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (great for surprises) | Companies like **Baker’s Box**, **Dessert Club**, or **Cratejoy** | Ideal for gifting or trying new flavors. | | **DIY kits** | All ingredients + instructions delivered | Sites like **HelloFresh**, **Blue Apron**, or specialty cake‑kit sites | Fun for a baking project; you’ll need a kitchen and oven. | ### Quick Steps to Order 1. **Decide on the type of cake** (birthday, wedding, custom design, ready‑made, etc.). 2. **Choose a provider** based on proximity, price, and style. 3. **Place the order**: most sites let you pick size, flavor, frosting, and add a personalized message. 4. **Confirm delivery details**: pick a pickup time or delivery window, and double‑check the address. 5. **Pay online** (most sites accept credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, etc.). ### Extra Tips - **Ask about allergies**: If you or your guests have dietary restrictions, many bakeries can accommodate gluten‑free, vegan, or nut‑free options. - **Check cancellation policies**: Some custom orders may have a non‑refundable fee if you cancel late. - **Read reviews**: Especially for online orders—look at photos and comments about taste, packaging, and delivery reliability. - **Plan ahead**: For special occasions, order at least a week in advance to secure your preferred cake and design. If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up specific bakeries or delivery services that operate in your area. Happy cake hunting! 🍰
